supersedes: the single placeholder BDD-000 created by the Control Center bootstrap
classification_note: Critical = the mission fails or actively misleads without it. High = the mission is materially weakened. Medium = quality/maintainability. Every BDD below asserts behaviour; none assert that a screen or field merely exists (Mission Clarification Gate).

scenarios.title: A project submits a single call and retrieves its result by ID
scenarios.given: Cortex is running and a calling project has a prompt to execute
scenarios.when: the project POSTs a single call and later polls the returned call ID
scenarios.then: submission returns a call ID immediately without blocking, the call reaches a terminal state, and polling the ID returns the output together with that same trace ID
scenarios.anti_demo: Must exercise the real HTTP API and a real provider, not an in-process function call.

scenarios.title: A job resolves to its per-call IDs and completes automatically
scenarios.given: a project submits a job containing several calls
scenarios.when: the job is submitted and then polled
scenarios.then: a job ID is returned that resolves to its per-call IDs, and the job completes automatically only when every constituent call is terminal — with partial completion retrievable rather than collapsed into a single 'failed'
scenarios.anti_demo: Partial completion must be asserted explicitly; a job reporting only success/failure fails this scenario.

scenarios.title: NAMED SCENARIO - live call under load: a call is served ahead of queued job work
scenarios.given: a batch job is queued and executing against the one-at-a-time local model
scenarios.when: a latency-sensitive call is submitted while the batch is in progress
scenarios.then: the call is dispatched at the next dispatch opportunity, ahead of all remaining job-calls, and does not wait for the batch to drain
scenarios.anti_demo: Must contend against a real queued batch, not a simulated delay.

scenarios.title: NAMED SCENARIO - machine sleep during a job: no work is lost
scenarios.given: a job is executing and one of its calls is leased to a worker
scenarios.when: the machine sleeps or the process is killed mid-call, and Cortex later restarts
scenarios.then: the leased call's lease expires and it returns to the queue rather than being stranded in 'executing', and the job resumes and completes
scenarios.anti_demo: An in-memory 'executing' flag cannot satisfy this. Requires a durable lease with an expiry, proven by an actual process kill and restart.

scenarios.title: Requeue after sleep does not double-charge a paid provider
scenarios.given: a call was already dispatched when the machine slept
scenarios.when: the lease expires and the call is requeued and retried
scenarios.then: recording is idempotent for that call ID, the trace shows both attempts distinctly, and the result is not duplicated into the job's output
scenarios.anti_demo: Cortex targets at-least-once delivery with idempotent recording; exactly-once must not be claimed.

scenarios.title: NAMED SCENARIO - quota exhaustion mid-batch: the chain fails over and records every switch
scenarios.given: a batch job is running against the configured provider chain
scenarios.when: the primary returns a real quota-exhaustion response mid-batch (Gemini 429/quota, or OpenRouter 'Rate limit exceeded: free-models-per-day')
scenarios.then: remaining calls continue on the next provider without caller change, and each attempt and switch is recorded in the trace with its reason
scenarios.anti_demo: Must reproduce exhaustion shapes actually observed in the Command Center's llm-usage.jsonl, not a generic 500.

scenarios.title: Every terminal call has a complete trace
scenarios.given: a mix of succeeded, failed, and exhausted calls have run
scenarios.when: the trace store is inspected
scenarios.then: every terminal call records input, output, model, provider, version, token counts, timing, status, and one record per provider attempt — with no partial or missing traces
scenarios.anti_demo: Traceability is the mission's product, not a log side-effect. A sampled or best-effort trace fails.

scenarios.title: The trace records what the model actually consumed, not just what was sent
scenarios.given: a call is executed against the local model
scenarios.when: the trace is written
scenarios.then: it records evaluated tokens (prompt_eval_count) alongside intended/sent tokens, and any call where evaluated < sent is recorded as a hard failure rather than a success
scenarios.anti_demo: Generation 0 proved a truncated call returns HTTP 200 with a plausible wrong answer. A trace recording only the sent prompt plus 'success' would be FALSE evidence.

scenarios.title: NAMED SCENARIO - trace lookup for a bad output attributes the fault to the prompt
scenarios.given: a call produced a bad output because its prompt was poorly written
scenarios.when: Ferosh looks up the returned trace ID via the API or the UI
scenarios.then: the trace shows the exact prompt, parameters, model, provider, and output — and is sufficient to conclude the prompt was at fault and to revise it
scenarios.anti_demo: The drill must end in an actual prompt revision, not just a rendered trace page.

scenarios.title: NAMED SCENARIO - a prompt overflowing the smallest context window fails clearly instead of truncating
scenarios.given: a client declared a required context window and submits a prompt exceeding the floor of the eligible handlers
scenarios.when: the call is routed and executed
scenarios.then: the call fails clearly with an explicit context-overflow error, and no truncated prompt is ever sent to a model
scenarios.anti_demo: MUST run against real Ollama or a fake reproducing the OBSERVED silent-truncation behaviour.

scenarios.title: The declared context window filters the eligible provider set before routing
scenarios.given: providers in the chain have different effective context windows
scenarios.when: a client declares a required window of N tokens
scenarios.then: only providers whose EFFECTIVE (configured, not advertised) window is >= N are eligible, the floor is computed over that filtered set, and a job no provider satisfies fails clearly rather than routing to a smaller model
scenarios.anti_demo: The eligibility filter must use effective windows. Advertised (131072) and effective (4096 default) differ by 32x.

scenarios.title: Cortex sets num_ctx explicitly per call and never inherits a provider default
scenarios.given: a call is dispatched to the local provider
scenarios.when: the request payload is inspected
scenarios.then: it carries an explicit num_ctx sized to the client's declared window, and the response's prompt_eval_count is asserted to match the intended token count
scenarios.anti_demo: Confirmed: default num_ctx evaluated 4096/10500 tokens and lost the needle; explicit num_ctx=16384 evaluated 12052 and recovered it.

scenarios.title: Fallback fires on availability failures only, never on content failures
scenarios.given: the provider chain is configured with a primary and fallbacks
scenarios.when: the primary returns (a) a 429/quota/timeout/transport error, versus (b) a reachable model returning a bad answer
scenarios.then: case (a) falls through to the next provider; case (b) does NOT fall through and is recorded as a quality signal against that model and prompt
scenarios.anti_demo: Falling back on content failure would burn the whole chain on one bad prompt AND launder a prompt defect into an availability event — destroying the mission's core signal.

scenarios.title: Work submitted while the machine is off is executed later, not rejected
scenarios.given: the local model is unavailable and no paid provider is eligible
scenarios.when: a project submits a call
scenarios.then: the call is accepted and queued with a retrievable status rather than rejected, and executes when a provider becomes available
scenarios.anti_demo: Must survive a restart between submission and execution.

scenarios.title: Background jobs keep advancing under continuous call load (fairness floor)
scenarios.given: a batch job is queued and calls arrive continuously
scenarios.when: the scheduler dispatches over a sustained period
scenarios.then: job-calls still make measurable progress against an explicit, configured fairness floor rather than being starved indefinitely
scenarios.assumption: OQ-4 unanswered: default floor set to 1 job-call guaranteed every 4th dispatch. Configurable.
scenarios.note: behaviour verified with default floor (every 4th dispatch) + disabled-floor control; the NUMBER is OQ-4.

scenarios.title: The dashboard surfaces an unreliable model at a glance
scenarios.given: one provider has an elevated failure and fallback rate across recent calls
scenarios.when: an agent inspects the rendered dashboard with no prior knowledge
scenarios.then: the agent can identify which model is unreliable and why, and the displayed aggregates reconcile exactly with values recomputed from raw traces
scenarios.anti_demo: A readable dashboard showing wrong numbers is worse than none (MISSION.md:92).

scenarios.title: Agent pre-review finds the screens uncrowded, non-redundant, and clear before Ferosh reviews
scenarios.given: the dashboard is rendered with realistic data
scenarios.when: an agent inspects the actual screens ahead of any human review
scenarios.then: it reports whether they are crowded, over-complicated, redundant, or unclear, and whether they actually show that the system is doing what it should — and Critical/High findings are resolved before Ferosh looks
scenarios.anti_demo: The agent must inspect rendered screens, not source code.

scenarios.title: INVERSE DRILL - a harness fault is not misattributed to the prompt
scenarios.given: a call produced a bad output because the harness silently truncated the prompt
scenarios.when: the trace for that call is inspected
scenarios.then: the trace makes the truncation visible (evaluated < sent) and the failure is attributable to the harness, NOT to the prompt
scenarios.anti_demo: This scenario protects the mission's central thesis. Without it, 'blame the prompt' becomes a way to blame the prompt for infrastructure bugs.
scenarios.note: Reinforced: an independent caller review confirmed the harness-vs-prompt distinction, and a boundary field-drop instance (HIGH-1) was fixed and covered by test/contract-guards.test.mjs.

scenarios.title: NDCG is correct against a known published reference
scenarios.given: retail-search's evaluation metrics carry published BM25 nDCG@10 sanity targets
scenarios.when: Cortex's NDCG path is run over reference data
scenarios.then: computed nDCG@10 matches known-correct values within tolerance
scenarios.anti_demo: Reuse retail-search/src/evaluation/metrics.js; a second, subtly-different NDCG is itself the plausible-but-wrong-numbers risk.

scenarios.title: LLM relevance judgments are stable enough to trust
scenarios.given: a fixed set of (query, product) pairs
scenarios.when: the same pairs are judged repeatedly at temperature 0
scenarios.then: judgment variance is measured and bounded, and grades are validated against the declared scale
scenarios.anti_demo: The metric math being right does not make the judgments right.
scenarios.note: query_id now required + unique; incomplete-judgment guard confirmed. Broader judge-variance study is a Gen-2 item.

scenarios.title: Switching provider requires no change in a calling project
scenarios.given: a caller submits an identical job twice
scenarios.when: the provider chain is reconfigured between runs
scenarios.then: the caller's code and request are unchanged, both runs return usable results, and the trace records which provider handled each
scenarios.anti_demo: Parity must be validated explicitly (MISSION.md:89).

scenarios.title: Cortex never writes into a consuming project's repository
scenarios.given: a Cortex session is running
scenarios.when: the session performs its work, including retrofit preparation
scenarios.then: no file outside the cortex repository is modified, and cross-repo work is expressed as a handoff artifact instead
scenarios.user_confirmation: Reaffirmed by Ferosh 2026-07-16: 'in mde, we don't modify other projects'. He will trigger the refactor from those projects himself.

removed_or_deferred.title: Engineering work requires the captured mission
removed_or_deferred.reason: Control Center placeholder. It asserts a process fact about the agent, not a real-world behaviour of Cortex, and would pass while the product did nothing.
